Subject: Tail-latency vs throughput: pilot path and next steps (hosted / dedicated)

Hi Avery / Samir — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can converge on a deployment mode that fits your SLA and budget constraints.

Recap (from call):
- Primary goal: conversational product for checkout help (inference calls per product page).
- Traffic shape: peak bursts ~450 QPS for 90s, baseline ~40 QPS.
- Latency SLO target: 95th <= 120ms for inference-only token throughput (end-to-end budget including network ~200ms).
- Message length: ~40 tokens avg, occasional longer contexts to 160 tokens.
- Data sensitivity: no PCI data in prompts; billing events stored in your backend — no additional compliance gating requested today.

Initial qualification notes:
- Hosted API can serve your baseline and short bursts using our burst pools, but at 95th=120ms during sustained 450 QPS bursts the unit cost and probability of hitting tail latency increases without reserved capacity.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) gives stronger control on 95/99 tail latency via fixed concurrency and KV cache locality; better for predictable peaks and can lower per-token cost under sustained throughput.
- Private VPC / on-prem not required based on current answers but remains an option if compliance demands change.

What we need from you to finalize recommendation:
1) Confirm a realistic 7-day sample of traffic (timezone, weekdays vs weekend) — CSV or perf snapshot. Your profiling file you promised would help (attached example column format in profiling_logs_timestamps.csv).
2) Confirm whether 95th=120ms is a hard requirement or a target band (eg. acceptable 95th up to 150ms during peak).
3) Any hard budget limits for monthly committed spend for Dedicated? If yes, state a target range.

Proposed action (my recommended path of least friction):
- Short-term: run Hosted API with K=adaptive batching + prefix KV caching enabled for 72h pilot to validate tail shape. This requires no contract.
- If 95th exceeds your target during the 72h or predicted cost is >20% above your target, move to a 2-week Dedicated pilot (we will pre-allocate capacity to match expected concurrent requests and provide SLA targets).

Requested next steps:
- Samir: please send the 7-day trace (or the metrics you can share) by EOD Wed.
- Avery: confirm acceptable 95th latency band and whether procurement can approve a 2-week paid pilot if needed.

I attached a short SLA proposal and an example profiler CSV to illustrate the fields we use for latency bucketing.

Thanks — I’ll stand up a Hosted pilot immediately once we get the trace and will include Ben and Markus on the runbook for measurement.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
--
